objective: Evaluate a feedback-complete SemWeaver refinement loop against the actual KNighter loop on all 12 fixed-noisy subjects, with a same-loop no-internal-evidence ablation and a 39-checker adopt-only portfolio view.
development_boundary: The v7 method and prompts were changed after inspecting complete v6 one-pass failures. The 12 subjects are development-informed, not a new held-out set. V6 and v7 are different treatments and must not be pooled.
replicate_plan: Rep01 uses the clean v6 rep01 KNighter strict baseline. Additional KNighter baseline manifests were frozen before their model calls, but their treatment caps cannot be frozen until those baselines complete. Rep01 is a full-cohort development evaluation; later repetitions, if run, estimate decode variability rather than untouched-subject generalization. Any omitted planned repetition must be recorded explicitly.
execution_order: Within rep01: pre-existing clean KNighter baseline and zero-model strict postvalidation, then native-evidence feedback loop, then no-internal feedback loop. Arms run sequentially because they share the Linux checkout.
model_identity_limit: Floating gateway alias with no immutable underlying model revision exposed.
credential_boundary: Read from a mode-0600 mounted private file; the key and local private path are never included in the release artifact.
method: Each subject inherits its paired KNighter successful model-call cap. One model edit attempt is followed by local gates and, if locally valid, external paired Linux object validation. Hash-bound compiler or paired feedback may enter the next model call only if the subject has cap remaining. Stop at first strict PDS. No manual repair is credited.
evidence_contrast: Both SemWeaver arms use identical starting checkers, prompts, model, call caps, feedback loop, and external validator. Native sees the frozen strictly internal record view and requires its origin gate; no-internal sees an empty record bundle and disables only that necessary entry gate. All 12 cases remain in both arms.
acceptance: Adopt only changed, compiling candidates with a positive vulnerable-side target hit and exactly zero fixed-side alerts under the same patch-related-object scope; otherwise retain the frozen starting checker. Candidate explanations or self-reported success are not outcome labels.
provider_cleanliness: SDK hidden retries and response-format fallback are disabled. HTTP 429 is retried on the same bound invocation with four attempts and 15, 30, then 60 seconds of backoff. Any observed retry/429 or binding fallback invalidates the affected arm and stops the batch before a method row; restart in a fresh directory, never count it as a checker failure.
reporting: Give all 12 per-case outcomes, call/token counts, paired validator counts, fixed-alert burden, time, and baseline-vs-native/native-vs-no-internal discordance. Repeated decodes of the same subjects are correlated and cannot be counted as independent patches. Version-level F1 uses the frozen 39 vulnerable and 39 fixed patch-version decisions, not individual alerts or unseen-code prevalence.
postfreeze: Any metamorphic or unrelated-edit tests occur after candidate freeze and cannot feed back into that same run. They diagnose patch-bound behavior, not method-level generalization superiority over KNighter.
stability: No prompt, evidence bundle, starting checker, parser, model, effort, feedback rule, gate, or validation-scope change during rep01 native and no-internal arms.
